the use of 1.00-m gadobutrole in patients with an indications for contrast-enhanced MR-angiography of supra-aortal or peripheral arteries is safe.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the safety of gadobutrol for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in patients with renal impairment and with the safety of intravascular contrast agents for MRI.
the safety of the new contrast medium 1.0 m gadobutrol for magnetic resonance angiography.
the safety of the contrast agent gadobutrol and its application in the clinical routine of magnetic resonance imaging.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gadobutrol is well tolerated in the doses applied and that the contrast agent is safe for the patients.
1.0 m gadobutrol has been proven to be a safe contrast medium in patients with an indicated contrast enhanced MR angiography.
1.0-M gadobutrol is a very safe contrast agent with a very good tolerance profile and no clinically relevant adverse events.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of gadobutrol as contrast agent for CE MRA of supra-aortal arteries, peripheral arteries, or pelvic arteries does not cause any clinically relevant adverse events.
the use of gadobutrol for contrast-enhanced MRI is safe and well tolerated in patients with normal and impaired renal function.

1.0 M gadolinium is a safe contrast material for CE MRA of supra-aortal and peripheral arteries.
1.0-M gadobutrol is safe and well tolerated.
